name: Trinidad and Tobago

facts.religion: Christian about 55%, Hindu about 18%, Muslim about 5%

snapshot: The Caribbean's energy powerhouse, where Kamla Persad-Bissessar returned as prime minister in 2025 and backed US strikes on Venezuelan boats nearby.
culture: Trinidad's Carnival is one of the world's great festivals, with calypso, soca and masquerade bands. The steelpan, made from oil drums in the 1930s, is the national instrument. Indo-Trinidadians, descended from indentured labourers, have made chutney music, Diwali and Phagwah part of national life. Cricket and Brian Lara are sources of pride.
society: Oil, gas and petrochemicals have made the country relatively wealthy, though output is declining. Gang violence has driven murders to record highs, prompting states of emergency. Politics largely splits between the Afro-Trinidadian-backed PNM and the Indo-Trinidadian-backed UNC.
baseline: Kamla Persad-Bissessar's United National Congress won the April 2025 election, returning her to the job she held from 2010 to 2015. She has aligned closely with the Trump administration's campaign against Venezuela's former government.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar, since May 2025
